subject: NeuroHealth: emergency rollback / retention safeguards + subprocessor approval
messages:
From: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@neurohealth.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: legal@neurohealth.com
Date: 2029-05-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Retention safeguards + subprocessor information request

Marcus —

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal has a couple of asks before we can sign the integration SOW and DPA: specifically around retention/backup purge timelines and an emergency rollback/circuit-breaker process tied to subcontractor (subprocessor) access. High level:

- We need a clear timeline for backups (how long snapshots are retained) and the process for emergency purges.
- We need to understand whether Redwood can implement a short-lived immutable snapshot window prior to deletion for forensic/rollback purposes (NeuroHealth requires the ability to request a rollback within X hours).
- We require a list of subprocessors (names, roles, regions) and confirmation of which subprocessors have access to backups and logs.
- For any deletion or purge, we need an emergency "escape hatch" process so NeuroHealth can pause a purge and request temporary retention for up to 14 days while an incident is investigated.

I attached a short questionnaire (NeuroHealth_DPA_questions.docx) and our preliminary redline expectations. Can you confirm whether your standard DPA already covers an operator-led circuit-breaker and what the timeline would look like for backup purge updates? Also, who at Redwood should be the security/ops point of contact for a rapid approval?

Sarah Lewis
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security
NeuroHealth Inc.
[Attachment: NeuroHealth_DPA_questions.docx (docx)]

From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@neurohealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2029-05-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention safeguards + subprocessor information request

Sarah —

Appreciate the clear asks. Short answer: yes, we can operationalize an "escape hatch" and provide a subprocessor breakdown; we also want to align on exact SLAs and approval authority so it's not a blocker during an incident. Proposed next steps from our side:

1) Immediate deliverables (today/T+1):
   - DataRetentionMatrix.xlsx (attached) — mapping of data types -> backup retention windows -> purge cadence -> available rollback windows.
   - subprocessors_list.csv (attached) — names, roles, regions, whether they have backup/log access.

2) Operational design (this week):
   - Circuit-breaker runbook: a documented flow that allows either party to pause scheduled purges for a named dataset for up to 14 days. Pause is triggered by a security request submitted to an on-call channel; approval requires sign-off from Redwood Security lead (karthik_iyer@redwood.com) and NeuroHealth security contact.
   - Immutable snapshot option: we can create a short-lived immutable snapshot (configurable; default suggestion 72 hours) that is kept off-cycle to allow for forensic investigation. We need to negotiate the exact window for EU-regulated datasets.

3) Contractual updates:
   - We will review NeuroHealth's redlines to the DPA and propose language that maps the operational runbook to a DPA annex (automated retention actions + manual pause authority + required evidence steps).

Quick answers to immediate questions:
- Standard backup purge cadence (hosted API): daily incremental logs retained 30 days; full snapshots retained 90 days; automated purge jobs run on a rolling basis with a 14-day reclaim grace window for restores. We can shorten/extend these for regulated cohorts.
- Subprocessors with backup/log access are highlighted in the attached CSV; we will update with contact-level personnel and locations where required.

I copied Kimberly (procurement/sales lead) and Karthik (security) so they can weigh in on contractual wording and the runbook. Can we set a short call (30 min) tomorrow to sync and review the DPA redline?

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: DataRetentionMatrix.xlsx (xlsx); subprocessors_list.csv (csv)]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2029-05-13T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention safeguards + subprocessor information request

Marcus / Kimberly —

Technical notes for the runbook and DPA annex (high level):

- Circuit-breaker mechanics: implement a named "Retention Hold" flag at the dataset level that prevents scheduled purge jobs from enqueuing deletion tasks. The hold should be auditable and require two attributes: (1) initiator identity, (2) reason code + expected hold expiration (max 14 days unless extended by mutual agreement).

- Logs and forensics: operational logs (API, access, admin actions) are retained for 90 days by default. We can carve a 180-day retention for audit-necessary customers under a paid tier. Any extension requests should specify the exact log classes (access logs, index logs, KV cache snapshots).

- Immutable snapshot: for EU datasets we should default to an immutable snapshot window of 72 hours (configurable). Note: implementing true immutability for snapshots requires coordination with the storage backend (we use an off-cluster object-store with versioned buckets). There's an R&D lead time (~2-3 weeks) to bake in automated snapshot immutability into the UI; short-term we can do a manual process triggered by ops during onboarding.

- Evidence & auditables: the runbook must produce an exportable audit bundle (snapshot id, retention hold ticket id, approval log, requestor identity). SOC2 evidence will reference these bundles.

I can draft the technical appendix for the DPA annex and attach a minimal schema for the audit bundle.

- Karthik
Lead, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@neurohealth.com>

Date: 2029-05-15T16:42:00-07:00

Marcus —

Thanks — this is helpful and aligned with our expectations. A couple of clarifications before we schedule the DPA call:

- NeuroHealth needs the contract to state the retention hold can be initiated by our Security lead and must not be unilaterally lifted by Redwood without documented cause and NeuroHealth approval.
- For EU personal data, we require a minimum immutable-snapshot window of 48 hours prior to purge; we can accept 72 hours if that's your operational default.
- Please upload the DataRetentionMatrix.xlsx and subprocessors_list.csv to the Drive link you shared and post the DocuSign DPA draft when ready. I've attached a redline (DPA_redline_NeuroHealth.pdf).

We'll review your proposed DPA annex and provide redline comments. Our legal can approve the emergency hold authority if we see the audit bundle schema and the on-call approval flow.

Proposed time: 2029-05-16 10:00 PT for a 30-minute sync (Marcus + Karthik + NeuroHealth Sec + NeuroHealth Legal). Confirm?

Best,
Sarah Lewis

NeuroHealth Inc.
